standard.legal_basis: Section 250, Health and Social Care Act 2012

entries.hazard_description: Legacy allergy data visibility requirements conflict between FLLD-CLIN-v2.md and FLLD-DM-v3.md, potentially exposing patients to inaccurate information.
causes: CLIN-11-R01: The Aurora Allergy & Intolerance clinical summary panel shall be unpopulated and empty at go-live for all migrated patients. FILE:FLLD-CLIN-v2.md|16|The Aurora Allergy & Intolerance clinical summary panel shall be unpopulated and empty at go-live for all migrated patients, to ensure unverified legacy data does not compromise acute prescribing decisions.

CLIN-11-R02: Legacy allergy data must never populate a clinical field. FILE:FLLD-CLIN-v2.md|19|Legacy allergy data must never populate a clinical field, because the Clinical Safety Group ruled it unsafe for prescribing due to inconsistent coding and unverified severity in the legacy PAS.

DM-04-R03: Migrated allergy records will be visible and active in the panel at go-live. FILE:FLLD-DM-v3.md|26|All migrated allergy records shall be rendered immediately visible and active in the Aurora Allergy & Intolerance clinical summary panel upon initial user login at go-live.
entries.clinical_effect: Patients may be exposed to inaccurate or unverified allergy information, potentially leading to adverse drug reactions or inappropriate treatment decisions.
proposed_controls: Review and reconcile conflicting requirements between FLLD-CLIN-v2.md and FLLD-DM-v3.md.
Implement a mechanism to ensure data accuracy and verification before displaying legacy allergy information.

evidence.excerpt: The Aurora Allergy & Intolerance clinical summary panel shall be unpopulated and empty at go-live for all migrated patients, to ensure unverified legacy data does not compromise acute prescribing decisions.
All migrated allergy records shall be rendered immediately visible and active in the Aurora Allergy & Intolerance clinical summary panel upon initial user login at go-live.

entries.severity_rationale: Raised from Considerable to Major: unverified severity on a live prescribing panel is not merely one input, it is the hazard (FLLD-DM-v3.md:32 explicitly declares its own severity "Unknown" on a field that stays active/visible on a live clinical panel, and this hazard's own evidence already cites that document).

entries.hazard_description: Defaulting allergy severity to 'Unknown' without clinical oversight contradicts established clinical guidelines.
causes: CLIN-11-R05: Allergy severity and adverse reaction manifestations shall be captured directly from the patient at first appointment. FILE:FLLD-CLIN-v2.md|28|Allergy severity and adverse reaction manifestations shall be captured directly from the patient at first appointment, never inferred or derived from automated algorithms or unverified historical free-text notes.

DM-04-R05: Severity defaults to 'Unknown' if not parsed from legacy notes. FILE:FLLD-DM-v3.md|32|the record shall be migrated with severity defaulted to "Unknown" and shall remain active and visible in the clinical summary panel pending review at the patient's next encounter.
entries.clinical_effect: Patients may be incorrectly classified as having an 'Unknown' allergy severity, potentially leading to inappropriate treatment or delayed recognition of a serious allergic reaction.
proposed_controls: Review and revise the data migration process to prevent automatic severity defaulting.
Implement a workflow for clinical review and verification of allergy severity upon patient encounter.

evidence.excerpt: Allergy severity and adverse reaction manifestations shall be captured directly from the patient at first appointment, never inferred or derived from automated algorithms or unverified historical free-text notes.
the record shall be migrated with severity defaulted to "Unknown" and shall remain active and visible in the clinical summary panel pending review at the patient's next encounter.

entries.hazard_description: Safeguarding notes for paediatric patients may be truncated due to character limits, with responsibility deflected to the PAS safeguarding lead.
causes: CHAT-13: Safeguarding notes may be truncated due to Row 10's 4000-character limit. FILE:teams-export.txt|13|The safeguarding flag on the CareTrak record for the Okafor child (NHS 621 903 4471) is held in CLINICAL_COMMENTS, not a coded field. If Row 10 truncates at 4000 characters the safeguarding note is at the end and will be cut. Who owns that?

CHAT-14: Responsibility deflected to PAS safeguarding lead. FILE:teams-export.txt|14|Not us, that's a PAS safeguarding question. Raise it with the safeguarding lead directly rather than here please, this channel is exported to the programme SharePoint.
entries.clinical_effect: Critical safeguarding information for paediatric patients may be lost, potentially leading to inadequate protection and increased risk of harm.
proposed_controls: Clarify ownership and responsibility for safeguarding note truncation risk.
Implement a solution to prevent truncation of safeguarding notes, such as increasing the character limit or using a coded field.

evidence.excerpt: The safeguarding flag on the CareTrak record for the Okafor child (NHS 621 903 4471) is held in CLINICAL_COMMENTS, not a coded field. If Row 10 truncates at 4000 characters the safeguarding note is at the end and will be cut. Who owns that?
Not us, that's a PAS safeguarding question. Raise it with the safeguarding lead directly rather than here please, this channel is exported to the programme SharePoint.
